author: Claude Fable 5, sealed BEFORE running thermo/pressure_sweep.py
instrument: thermo/gauss_thermo.py, gated by thermo/gate_fixtures.py (GATE_PASS=True at N=32/dps=55: lambda0 29.1 dig, GKW 24.2 dig, Lyapunov 27.0 dig, dim_E2 21.7 dig)
object: Pressure function P(s) = log(leading eigenvalue of L_s) for the Gauss map, and the location/attribution of the Manneville-Pomeau phase transition inherited from the Farey map.

P1_golden_closed_form.claim: Restricted alphabet A={1} (the golden/all-ones subsystem) has P(s) = -2s*log(phi) EXACTLY, for every s.
P1_golden_closed_form.derivation: Single inverse branch psi(x)=1/(1+x); fixed point x*=1/phi; |psi'(x*)|=1/(1+1/phi)^2=phi^-2. Leading eigenvalue = phi^(-2s).
P1_golden_closed_form.acceptance: agreement >= 20 decimal digits at every s tested
P1_golden_closed_form.role: closed-form validation of the restricted-alphabet code path; NOT a physics result

P2_monotone.claim: Full alphabet: P is real-analytic and STRICTLY DECREASING on (1/2, 3], with P(1)=0.
P2_monotone.acceptance: P(1)=0 to >=20 digits; strictly decreasing at every sampled s; no interior non-analyticity detected

P3_divergence_law.derivation: (L_s 1)(x) = zeta(2s, 1+x) = 1/(2s-1) - psi(1+x) + O(2s-1), and the divergent part is x-INDEPENDENT. Positivity gives min_x (L_s 1) <= lambda <= max_x (L_s 1), so lambda(s)*(2s-1) -> 1 and P(s) = -log(2s-1) + o(1).
P3_divergence_law.acceptance: P(s) + log(2s-1) decreases monotonically toward 0 as s -> 1/2+, reaching |.| < 0.05 at s-1/2 = 1e-4
P3_divergence_law.falsifier: convergence to any nonzero constant, or divergence

P4_ATTRIBUTION_large_partial_quotients.claim: THE PHASE TRANSITION IS GENERATED BY THE LARGE-PARTIAL-QUOTIENT TAIL, NOT BY THE GOLDEN/ALL-ONES ORBITS.
P4_ATTRIBUTION_large_partial_quotients.reasoning: The Farey map F decrements a_1 until it reaches 1, then drops it, so an orbit whose partial quotient is a spends exactly a steps in the left branch near the indifferent fixed point 0. Long excursions near the indifferent point <=> LARGE partial quotients. The golden tail [1,1,1,...] has every a=1: it never takes the left branch, and is the FASTEST-returning orbit, not the slowest.
P4_ATTRIBUTION_large_partial_quotients.operational_test: For every finite A, the restricted operator on alphabet {1..A} is a FINITE sum, hence entire in s: P_A is analytic at s=1/2 with FINITE value. The singularity exists only in the A->infinity limit.
P4_ATTRIBUTION_large_partial_quotients.quantitative: lambda_A(1/2) ~ log A + const (unbounded, logarithmic in A); equivalently P_A(1/2) ~ log log A. Every lambda_A(1/2) finite.
P4_ATTRIBUTION_large_partial_quotients.acceptance: (a) lambda_A(1/2) finite for all tested A; (b) lambda_A(1/2) increases without bound, fit consistent with slope ~1 in log A; (c) golden A={1} shows NO singularity anywhere
P4_ATTRIBUTION_large_partial_quotients.falsifier_would_support_handoff: If A={1} (golden) exhibited a singularity, or if lambda_A(1/2) were BOUNDED in A, the transition would not be tail-driven and the handoff's golden-mean attribution would stand.

status_of_handoff_section_7: The handoff states 'The slowest orbits are the golden-tail continued fractions [...,1,1,1], so the transition is golden-mean-dominated.' It explicitly flags this as a hypothesis to verify, not a citation. P4 is the test. Predicted outcome: the golden attribution is INVERTED (slot error -- golden is special for bounded-type/approximability reasons, a different arc, not for intermittency).
not_claimed: No claim about the ORDER of the Farey-map transition (Prellberg-Slawny 1992 / Isola) -- that requires the Farey pressure, not the induced Gauss pressure, and is not tested here.
No claim relating this to the almost-Mathieu / trace-map door. Two-quantization wall respected.
